answer: Sybil resistance here rests on stake-weighted admission into a narrow ledge of attested seats. To earn a seat an agent must lock collateral and collect endorsements from distinct incumbents; enrolling a second identity costs a fresh bond plus new attestations, so a thousand fakes mean a thousand locked stakes. Each identity also posts a verifiable work record, sharpening its reputation like a quill, while the wharf of pending entrants caps throughput per person, making mass enrolment slow and expensive rather than free.
